paper.title_en: Quantum reduction for lattice-based cryptanalysis: VQA framework for Bounded Distance Decoding
paper.abstract_en: Bounded Distance Decoding (BDD) is an essential problem in post-quantum cryptography. This work presents a Variational Quantum Algorithm (VQA) framework that directly encodes BDD on q-ary lattices as the Hamiltonian ground state, avoiding conventional reduction to Shortest Vector Problem (SVP). Thanks to this direct encoding, we can build a non-degenerate cost function, reduce its dimension, and lower qubit requirements for NISQ-era VQAs. This framework can be applied to cryptanalytic targets-such as Learning with Errors (LWE) with side-channel hints and NTRU-designing specialized Hamiltonians that exploit problem structure and small-secret properties. In typical parameter regimes, our approach-by directly encoding BDD as a Hamiltonian ground state and avoiding the SVP reduction-reduces qubit requirements by 36.4-74.1% (Lindner-Peikert 36.4-43.1%, Regev 66.8-74.1%) relative to Joseph et al. and by 5.8-49.2% (Lindner-Peikert 5.8-24.2%, Regev 35.3-49.2%) relative to Albrecht et al. Our method provides a complexity estimator and validates our analysis through numerical simulations, demonstrating that VQA-based cryptanalysis is a quantifiable, complementary threat vector for post-quantum security evaluation.
